chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Umar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'We have young women and young men who are unable to fast due to the intensity of the thirst that strikes them.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let them drink by the measure that quenches their souls and what they are cautious of (from harm/exhaustion).'

key_terms.يَحْذَرُونَ: They are cautious of (fear of harm)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for the weak or elderly who cannot fast due to severe thirst?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of *La Darar wa La Dirar* (no harm) by permitting the weak to drink only enough to quench thirst and prevent danger, rather than requiring full hydration or complete exemption. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on proportionality in *Rukhas* (concessions), ensuring that the obligation of fasting does not become a burden that leads to actual harm. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the limits of endurance in worship, balancing spiritual discipline with physical preservation.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus, from Al Mufazzal Bin Umar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that we have young women and young men who are not able upon the Fasting from the intensity of what hits them from the thirst. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So let them drink by a measurement of what their selves can be quenched with and what they are being cautious of’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from ‘Isma‘il ibn Marrar from Yunus from al-Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of our young women and man who are not able to fast because of thirst. He (the Imam) said, ‘They can drink to quench their souls and to remove their fear.’”
